Our first-ever productivity challenge is live on YouTube: The CODE Challenge.

We gave three Second Brainers 30 days to put the CODE method under real pressure. Three different tools. Three projects with hard deadlines. One shared system: Capture, Organize, Distill, Express.

Episode 1 sets up the series. The next four episodes go deep on each step: Capture, Organize, Distill, Express.

Link in bio!
I'm kind of neurodivergent and just having a hard time focusing. Like three nights a week I sleep at like 3:00, 4:00 AM just working late. I don't even know if this is a good article. My mom got a little too close, and the manager got a little sussed out. If I need to work 18 hours a day to make this a success, I will do that. I'll make that happen. I don't even know if it's going to work. Just show me the sources, show me where it's coming from. Uh, or feeling stuck, overwhelmed. I'll get lost, man. I'll get lost researching, comparing myself to other people. Yeah, I hear you. That's good. That is good. Let's go with that. Let's go with that. Um uh, let's see here. I'll We gave three people 30 days to use the CODE method, a four-step framework created by Tiago Forte to manage information and boost productivity. It is supposed to help individuals systematically collect insights, arrange them, find the core essence, and generate creative work. It sounds good in theory, but can it hold up under the stress of actual deadlines and deep psychological friction? We decided to put it to the test. Three real people, 30 days, with completely different projects.

yourself I always get questions comments from you guys from my friends how do you get so much done in a day how are you so productive I wear a lot of different hats I have a full time job in corporate finance I teach fitness I obviously do social media I travel a lot I'm in a relationship yada yada all the things we're all super busy it's all about working smarter not harder I would not be where I am today be able to do all these different things to fill myself in different areas of my life if it weren't for these structured habits that I have honestly just implemented over the years they're like second nature to me now number one wake up earlier than you think you need to I'm not saying wake up early I'm not a 5 a m girl I've tried it I wish I was honestly I'm not there yet I'm like a 6:30 if you wake up at 9 a m 10 a m every day I'm not saying set your alarm for 5 a m like you're just gonna get tired and fail wake up earlier than you originally or initially think you need to say you have to be somewhere at 8 you set your alarm for 7 no set your alarm for 6:45 those 10 to 15 extra minutes will change your life it will tell your brain that we're waking up and we're being productive you can use the time for yourself take 15 minutes drink your coffee maybe you want to start a little laundry maybe you want to read a chapter of your book all I know is it sets the tone for the day I have been doing this for years I always set the alarm just a little bit earlier even if I'm exhausted I never ever regret it number two I will preach this till the day I die task management knock the bigger tasks out first focus on the aspects in your to do list that are actually moving the needle and will make big strides in your day your week your month I used to be the person that would like tackle all the little check marks off my to do list because it would make me feel better yeah I get it if that's what you need to do to like make yourself feel better and jump start your day that's fine but if you can knock out like 10% of a bigger task that is so much more beneficial in the long run than knocking out like 50 bajillion of the tiny little mundane like stupid tasks that
